quote: Every vulnerable example ships with its fixed version and an automated test proving the fix.
statement: In projects/security/**, every vulnerable example must be accompanied by a fixed version and an automated test that proves the fix.

quote: No payloads aimed at real systems, no evasion techniques, no attack tooling reusable outside the lab.
statement: In projects/security/**, code must not contain payloads aimed at real systems, evasion techniques or attack tooling reusable outside the lab.

quote: Load and performance tests never target third-party URLs.
statement: In load and performance test scripts (k6 and similar), code must not target third-party URLs.

quote: `.claude/skills/` holds Markdown only. Never add scripts, hooks or installers from the source repositories of those skills.
statement: In .claude/skills/**, only Markdown (plus LICENSE) files may exist; scripts, hooks, installers or binaries must not be added.

quote: Hooks are disabled for this project (`disableAllHooks` in `.claude/settings.local.json`). Do not re-enable them.
statement: Claude Code hooks must stay disabled for this project (disableAllHooks in .claude/settings.local.json).

quote: Code, identifiers and commit messages are in English.
statement: In all source files, code and identifiers must be written in English.

quote: Didactic code comments are trilingual: English, Portuguese and Spanish (see `.claude/rules/code-style.md`).
statement: In all source files, didactic code comments must be written in English, Portuguese and Spanish.

quote: **Indentation:** tabs, width 4 (see `.editorconfig`). Languages whose standard formatter enforces spaces follow the formatter.
statement: In all source files, indentation must use tabs (width 4), except languages whose standard formatter enforces spaces.

quote: **Dependencies:** pin exact stable versions. No `latest`, `next`, `rc`, `beta` or `alpha`.
statement: In package manifests (package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, requirements, etc.), dependencies must be pinned to exact stable versions; no latest, next, rc, beta, alpha or open ranges.

quote: Docker images use fixed version tags.
statement: In Dockerfiles and docker-compose files, images must reference a fixed version tag (never latest or an untagged image).

quote: **JS/TS package manager:** Bun.
statement: JS/TS projects must use Bun as the package manager.

quote: A trilingual README (`README.md`, `README.pt-BR.md`, `README.es.md`) explaining what it teaches
statement: In projects/<area>/<mini-project>/, the folder must contain README.md, README.pt-BR.md and README.es.md.

quote: `setup-unix-<project>.sh` and `setup-windows-<project>.ps1`
statement: In projects/<area>/<mini-project>/, the folder must contain setup scripts named setup-unix-<project>.sh and setup-windows-<project>.ps1.

quote: Automated tests that pass locally
statement: In projects/<area>/<mini-project>/, each mini-project must include automated tests.

quote: Code comments are **didactic, trilingual (English, Portuguese and Spanish) and written for beginners**. English stays the main language of the project and comes first.
statement: In all source files, didactic comments must be trilingual blocks with English first, then Portuguese, then Spanish, prefixed EN:, PT:, ES:.

quote: Explain the concept and the reason, not the syntax. Write one block per concept, with the three languages in the order `EN`, `PT`, `ES`, not a translation of every line.
statement: In all source files, trilingual comments must be written as one EN/PT/ES block per concept, not a line-by-line translation of each code line.

quote: Every place that has Portuguese has Spanish too: comments, READMEs (`README.es.md` next to `README.pt-BR.md`), `docs/es/` next to `docs/pt/`, and the `es` block of every quiz question.
statement: In all source files, every PT: comment block must be followed by an ES: comment block.

quote: Spanish is neutral Latin American Spanish (`tú`, not `vos` or `vosotros`).
statement: In Spanish comments and texts, wording must be neutral Latin American Spanish using tú, not vos or vosotros.

quote: Strong typing: no `any` (use `unknown` and narrow)
statement: In TypeScript files, code must not use the any type; use unknown and narrow instead.

quote: explicit return types on exported functions.
statement: In TypeScript files, exported functions must declare explicit return types.

quote: Never silence an error with `@ts-ignore` or by disabling a test.
statement: In TypeScript files, code must not use @ts-ignore to silence errors.

quote: Never silence an error with `@ts-ignore` or by disabling a test.
statement: In test files, tests must not be disabled or skipped (e.g. test.skip, xit) to silence a failure.

quote: Validate every external input (JSON files, HTTP bodies, environment variables) at the boundary with **Zod**, the default schema library of this repository
statement: In TypeScript code, every external input (JSON files, HTTP bodies, environment variables) must be validated at the boundary with a Zod schema.
scope: **/*.ts boundary code (file readers, HTTP handlers, env loading)

quote: Derive the TypeScript types from the schemas with `z.infer` instead of writing them twice.
statement: In TypeScript code, types for validated data must be derived from Zod schemas with z.infer rather than declared separately.

quote: Do not hand-write validators.
statement: In TypeScript code, input validators must not be hand-written; use Zod schemas.

quote: Never commit secrets, `.env` files, Terraform state, or `.claude/settings.local.json`.
statement: The repository must not contain secrets, .env files, Terraform state or .claude/settings.local.json.

quote: k6 and similar tools target **only local services** created in this repository (`localhost` or docker-compose service names). Never a third-party URL.
statement: In k6 and similar load-test scripts, targets must be localhost or docker-compose service names of this repository, never a third-party URL.

quote: The target comes from a variable that defaults to a local address. Scripts must refuse to run when the host is not local.
statement: In load-test scripts, the target host must come from a variable defaulting to a local address, and the script must refuse to run when the host is not local.

quote: Cross-language benchmarks follow one contract: every implementation reads the same input and prints JSON with at least `n`, elapsed time and memory.
statement: In cross-language benchmark implementations, each implementation must read the same input and print JSON containing at least n, elapsed time and memory.

quote: Results are committed as text or Markdown tables. Raw output folders such as `k6-results/` stay git-ignored.
statement: Benchmark results must be committed as text or Markdown tables, and raw output folders such as k6-results/ must stay git-ignored.

quote: Mini-projects live in `projects/<area>/<mini-project>/`, with one subfolder per language (`ts/`, `go/`, `rust/`). TypeScript is the reference implementation
statement: Mini-projects must live in projects/<area>/<mini-project>/ with one subfolder per language (ts/, go/, rust/, ...), and include a TypeScript reference implementation.

quote: Three READMEs explaining what it teaches: `README.md` in English, `README.pt-BR.md` in Portuguese and `README.es.md` in Spanish, each linking to the other two on the line under the title.
statement: Each mini-project README (EN, PT-BR, ES) must link to the other two on the line under the title.

quote: The dashboard is a static page (HTML + Tailwind CSS v4 reading the results JSON). Next.js only where the concept needs a server.
statement: In mini-project dashboards, the UI must be a static HTML page with Tailwind CSS v4 reading the results JSON; Next.js may be used only where the concept needs a server.

quote: Setup scripts named `setup-unix-<project>.sh` and `setup-windows-<project>.ps1`. Everything runs in Docker with pinned images, so the scripts require only Docker.
statement: Mini-project setup scripts must be named setup-unix-<project>.sh and setup-windows-<project>.ps1 and run everything in Docker with pinned images, requiring only Docker on the host.

quote: Tailwind CSS v4 for web interfaces, with Base UI (`@base-ui/react`, unstyled) for the interactive components of React interfaces.
statement: In React interfaces, interactive components must use Base UI (@base-ui/react) and styling must use Tailwind CSS v4.

quote: Docker images use a fixed version tag. Prefer the official `oven/bun` images for JS/TS projects.
statement: In Dockerfiles of JS/TS projects, the base image should be an official oven/bun image with a fixed version tag.

quote: JS/TS uses Bun unless the mini-project is specifically about Node.js/npm.
statement: In JS/TS mini-projects, code must run on Bun unless the mini-project is specifically about Node.js/npm.

quote: Ask the owner before adding a dependency that is not in the stack above.
statement: Dependencies outside the listed stack must not be added without the owner's approval.

quote: Start from `bun run new:project <area> <name> --langs ...`, with the name and path listed in `quiz/content/mini-projects.json`, and set `status` to `"done"` there when the mini-project is finished.
statement: Each mini-project must be listed with its path in quiz/content/mini-projects.json, with status "done" once finished.

quote: Commit `setup-unix-<name>.sh` with the executable bit: `git update-index --chmod=+x <file>`.
statement: setup-unix-<name>.sh scripts must be committed with the executable bit set.

quote: PowerShell setup scripts use `$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"` and check `$LASTEXITCODE` after each step
statement: In setup-windows-*.ps1 scripts, code must set $ErrorActionPreference = "Continue" and check $LASTEXITCODE after each step.

quote: A static dashboard commits its built `tailwind.css`.
statement: In static dashboards, the built tailwind.css must be committed next to the page.

quote: The page loads data through `<script src>` files, not `fetch`, so it works when opened from disk.
statement: In static dashboard pages, data must be loaded through <script src> files, not fetch().

quote: Use the benchmark runner (`bench.json` and `bun run bench`) when the lesson is time or memory of a process. A deterministic simulation (page faults, comparison counts, fragmentation) writes its own table to `results/`
statement: Mini-projects whose lesson is process time or memory should define a bench.json for the benchmark runner; deterministic simulations should write their own table to results/.

quote: A mini-project never imports code from another one. Copy what it needs and say so in the README.
statement: In projects/<area>/<mini-project>/**, code must not import code from another mini-project's folder.

quote: Playwright: the package and the Docker image must have the same version.
statement: Where Playwright is used, the playwright package version must match the Playwright Docker image tag.

quote: Unique docker-compose project name, no fixed host port unless the demo needs one (then bound to `127.0.0.1`), and `docker compose down -v` at the end of a test run.
statement: In docker-compose files, the project name must be unique and no fixed host port may be published unless the demo needs it, in which case it must be bound to 127.0.0.1.

quote: and `docker compose down -v` at the end of a test run.
statement: In setup/test scripts that start docker compose, the run must end with docker compose down -v.

quote: **Containers that write into the mounted project folder run as the host user**: `user: "${HOST_UID:-1000}:${HOST_GID:-1000}"` in docker-compose, with `HOST_UID="$(id -u)"` and `HOST_GID="$(id -g)"` exported by the Unix setup script.
statement: In docker-compose files, containers that write into the mounted project folder must set user: "${HOST_UID:-1000}:${HOST_GID:-1000}", and the Unix setup script must export HOST_UID and HOST_GID.

quote: PostgreSQL: `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U <user> -d <db>`, over TCP, because during initialisation the server answers on the Unix socket only and then restarts.
statement: In docker-compose PostgreSQL health checks, the check must be pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U <user> -d <db> (over TCP).

quote: RabbitMQ: `nc -z 127.0.0.1 5672`, not `rabbitmq-diagnostics`
statement: In docker-compose RabbitMQ health checks, the check must be nc -z 127.0.0.1 5672 and must not use rabbitmq-diagnostics.

quote: App in `quiz/`: Next.js with static site generation (SSG), Base UI (`@base-ui/react`) for the interactive components and Tailwind CSS v4 for the styling, no back end. Progress is stored in the browser.
statement: In quiz/, the app must be a statically generated Next.js app with no back end (no API routes or server runtime); progress is stored in the browser.

quote: Interactive controls (buttons, toggles, selects, meters, popups) are Base UI components styled with Tailwind classes built from the theme tokens of `quiz/src/app/globals.css`, never a raw colour and never a hand-rolled widget
statement: In quiz/src/**, interactive controls (buttons, toggles, selects, meters, popups) must be @base-ui/react components, not hand-rolled widgets.

quote: styled with Tailwind classes built from the theme tokens of `quiz/src/app/globals.css`, never a raw colour
statement: In quiz/src/**, styling must use Tailwind classes built from the theme tokens of quiz/src/app/globals.css and must not use raw colour values.

quote: Links stay links, and static markup is not wrapped in Base UI.
statement: In quiz/src/**, links must remain plain links and static markup must not be wrapped in Base UI components.

quote: Three features are mandatory: i18n in English, Portuguese and Spanish, a light and dark theme toggle, and a mobile-friendly layout (usable from 320 px wide).
statement: In quiz/, the app must provide i18n in English, Portuguese and Spanish, a light/dark theme toggle and a layout usable from 320 px wide.

quote: Questions in `quiz/content/<area>/<topic>.json`, validated by a schema.
statement: Quiz questions must live in quiz/content/<area>/<topic>.json and conform to the question schema.

quote: Every question has exactly **5 alternatives**, one correct, a difficulty (`basic`, `intermediate`, `advanced`), a `source` (book or lecture and chapter) and, when one exists, the related `miniProject`.
statement: In quiz/content/<area>/<topic>.json, every question must have exactly 5 alternatives with one correct, a difficulty of basic/intermediate/advanced, a source, and a miniProject when one exists.

quote: Every question is written in **English, Portuguese and Spanish** at the same time (blocks `en`, `pt`, `es`). The schema refuses a question with a missing language.
statement: In quiz question JSON, every question must have en, pt and es blocks.

quote: The explanation has: the concept and why the right alternative is right, one line for **each** wrong alternative, an optional code example or diagram, and links to the mini-project and the source.
statement: In quiz question JSON, the explanation must cover the concept, why the right alternative is right, and one line for each wrong alternative.

quote: Screen: one question per screen, two-column grid, question and alternatives on the left, explanation on the right after the answer. Columns stack on a phone.
statement: In the quiz question screen, the layout must show one question per screen in a two-column grid (question/alternatives left, explanation right after answering) that stacks on phones.

quote: **A statement never depends on `example`.** The example belongs to the explanation and is shown only after the answer. Code, tables, graphs or schedules needed to answer go in `snippet`
statement: In quiz question JSON, the statement must not depend on the example field; material needed to answer must be in snippet or the statement.

quote: **Correct index**: spread it evenly and pseudo-randomly over 0 to 4. A fixed rotation (+1 per question) is a pattern a student can learn.
statement: In quiz question JSON, the answer index should be spread evenly and pseudo-randomly over 0 to 4, never in a fixed rotation.

quote: **Length**: the correct alternative must not be the longest more often than chance (about 20%).
statement: In quiz question JSON, the correct alternative must not be the longest one in more than about 20% of an area's questions.

quote: **SEO files are generated, never hand-edited.** `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` come from `quiz/src/app/` at every `next build` ... Do not add files under `quiz/public/` for them.
statement: In quiz/, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, llms.txt and llms-full.txt must be generated from quiz/src/app/ (builders in quiz/src/lib/seo.ts) and must not be added as files under quiz/public/.

quote: Use an `internal: true` network in docker-compose and bind published ports to `127.0.0.1`.
statement: In security lab docker-compose files, services must use an internal: true network and published ports must be bound to 127.0.0.1.

quote: Every vulnerable example ships together with its **fixed version** and an **automated test** that fails against the vulnerable code and passes against the fix.
statement: In projects/security/**, each vulnerable example must have a fixed version and an automated test that fails against the vulnerable code and passes against the fix.

quote: Not allowed: payloads aimed at real systems, evasion techniques (WAF, EDR, antivirus, detection bypass), and attack tools that are reusable outside the lab.
statement: In projects/security/**, code must not include payloads aimed at real systems, WAF/EDR/antivirus evasion, or attack tools reusable outside the lab.

quote: Vulnerable code is clearly labelled as such in file names, comments and the README
statement: In projects/security/**, vulnerable code must be labelled as vulnerable in its file names and comments.

quote: and is never importable as a library by other mini-projects.
statement: Vulnerable code in projects/security/** must not be imported by other mini-projects.

quote: No real credentials, tokens or personal data, even as examples. Use obviously fake values.
statement: In security labs, code and fixtures must not contain real credentials, tokens or personal data; only obviously fake values.

quote: Go `misspell` reads Spanish words as English typos: add them to `ignore-rules` in the module's `.golangci.yml`.
statement: In Go modules, Spanish/Portuguese comment words flagged by misspell must be added to ignore-rules in that module's .golangci.yml rather than changing the comments.

quote: `clang-format`, `ruff` (100 columns), `gofmt` and google-java-format reflow or reject long comment lines, so wrap an `ES:` block like its `PT:` block
statement: In source files, ES: comment blocks must be wrapped like their PT: block to fit the formatter's line length (e.g. ruff 100 columns).

quote: **Theory summary** of every quiz area in `quiz/content/<area>/theory/{en,pt,es}.json` ... The three languages must share one skeleton ... Table headers cannot be empty, and `*italic*` is not a mark (use `**bold**`).
statement: Each quiz area must have quiz/content/<area>/theory/en.json, pt.json and es.json with the same skeleton; table headers must not be empty and *italic* must not be used (use **bold**).

quote: its `workflow-sync` test fails when `ci.yml` gains a named step that the lesson does not demonstrate: a new gate needs a `demo/<gate>/` folder, the runner case and the READMEs.
statement: Every named step in .github/workflows/ci.yml must have a matching demo/<gate>/ folder and runner case in projects/continuous-integration/ci-pipeline.

quote: Bun closes a connection silent for 10 seconds, so a long request needs `idleTimeout`.
statement: In Bun servers that serve long requests, Bun.serve must set idleTimeout above the request duration.

quote: A watcher that reads a Prometheus ratio must treat `NaN` (0 / 0, no traffic yet) as a missing sample (`slo-alert`).
statement: In code reading Prometheus ratios, NaN results must be treated as a missing sample.

quote: The file name is the topic slug, and it must exist in `coverage.json`.
statement: Each quiz/content/<area>/<topic>.json file must be named after a topic slug that exists in that area's coverage.json.

quote: The topics and the targets come from the table of the area in `PLAN.md`. The targets add up to the target of the area.
statement: In quiz/content/<area>/coverage.json, topic targets must add up to the area target.

quote: `id` | `<area>-<topic>-<nn>`, unique in the whole quiz, never reused.
statement: In quiz question JSON, id must follow <area>-<topic>-<nn> and be unique across the whole quiz.

quote: `difficulty` | `basic`, `intermediate` or `advanced`. Aim for 40%, 40% and 20% in each area
statement: In each quiz area, question difficulties should be distributed about 40% basic, 40% intermediate and 20% advanced.

quote: `answer` | index of the correct alternative, 0 to 4. Spread the correct position: no index should hold more than about 30% of an area
statement: In quiz question JSON, answer must be an index 0-4, and no index should hold more than about 30% of an area's answers.

quote: `miniProject` | optional. A path listed in `mini-projects.json`. Required when the concept is shown by a mini-project
statement: In quiz question JSON, miniProject must be a path listed in quiz/content/mini-projects.json, and is required when a mini-project shows the concept.

quote: `alternatives` | exactly 5, all different, one correct
statement: In quiz question JSON, alternatives must contain exactly 5 distinct entries with exactly one correct.

quote: `explanations` | exactly 5, in the same order: explanation `i` says why alternative `i` is right or wrong
statement: In quiz question JSON, explanations must contain exactly 5 entries, in the same order as alternatives.

quote: `snippet` | optional code or text diagram that the student must read to answer. ... Present in all three languages or in none
statement: In quiz question JSON, snippet must be present in all three language blocks (en, pt, es) or in none.

quote: `example` | optional code (`kind: "code"`, with `language`) or text diagram (`kind: "diagram"`). Present in all three languages or in none
statement: In quiz question JSON, example must be kind "code" with a language or kind "diagram", present in all three language blocks or in none.

quote: Avoid "all of the above", "none of the above", and pairs that are both right depending on the reading.
statement: In quiz question JSON, alternatives should not use "all of the above" or "none of the above".

quote: **No trick wording.** Avoid double negatives, and write "NOT" or "EXCEPT" in capitals when a question asks for the wrong item.
statement: In quiz question statements, NOT or EXCEPT must be written in capitals when the question asks for the wrong item.

quote: Keep code, identifiers and established technical terms identical in all of them.
statement: In quiz question JSON, code, identifiers and technical terms must be identical across the en, pt and es blocks.

quote: At least 3 sections. The `id` is an English kebab-case slug, unique in the file.
statement: In quiz/content/<area>/theory/*.json, there must be at least 3 sections, each with an English kebab-case id unique in the file.

quote: The three languages have the same skeleton: the same section ids in the same order and, in each section, the same block types in the same order. Only the words change.
statement: In quiz/content/<area>/theory/{en,pt,es}.json, the three files must have the same section ids in the same order and the same block types in the same order per section.

quote: `table` | `headers`, `rows`, optional `caption` | side by side comparison. Every row has one cell per header
statement: In theory summary table blocks, every row must have exactly one cell per header.

quote: `video` | `title`, `url` (https) | a link to a video ... It is a link, not an embedded player
statement: In theory summary video blocks, url must be https and the video must be rendered as a link, not an embedded player.

quote: Inside any text four marks are read, and nothing else (HTML stays as plain text): `**bold**`, `` `code` ``, `[text](https://...)` and `[[term|meaning]]`
statement: In quiz theory text, only the marks **bold**, `code`, [text](https://...) and [[term|meaning]] may be used, and HTML must be rendered as plain text.

quote: "linter": { "enabled": true, "rules": { "preset": "recommended", "suspicious": { "noExplicitAny": "error" } } }
statement: In JS/TS files covered by Biome, code must not use an explicit any type.

quote: select = ["E", ...] (pycodestyle errors)
statement: In Python files, code must pass ruff pycodestyle error rules (E); the same family is selected in every projects/**/python/ruff.toml.

quote: select = [..., "F", ...] (pyflakes)
statement: In Python files, code must pass ruff pyflakes rules (F): no unused imports/variables, undefined names, etc.

quote: select = [..., "W", ...] (pycodestyle warnings)
statement: In Python files, code must pass ruff pycodestyle warning rules (W).

quote: select = [..., "I", ...] (isort)
statement: In Python files, imports must be sorted per ruff isort rules (I).

quote: select = [..., "B", ...] (flake8-bugbear)
statement: In Python files, code must pass ruff flake8-bugbear rules (B), e.g. no mutable default arguments.

quote: select = [..., "UP", ...] (pyupgrade)
statement: In Python files, code must use modern syntax per ruff pyupgrade rules (UP) for target-version py314.

quote: select = [..., "SIM", ...] (flake8-simplify)
statement: In Python files, code must pass ruff flake8-simplify rules (SIM).

quote: select = [..., "ANN"] (flake8-annotations)
statement: In Python files, functions must have type annotations for arguments and return values (ruff ANN).

quote: ignore = ["EXE002"]
statement: In projects/**/python/*.py, ruff EXE002 (executable file without shebang) is turned off in all 18 per-project ruff.toml files.

quote: enable: - errorlint
statement: In Go files, error comparisons and type assertions must use errors.Is/errors.As and %w wrapping (golangci-lint errorlint).

quote: enable: - gocritic
statement: In Go files, code must pass golangci-lint gocritic checks.

quote: enable: - revive
statement: In Go files, code must pass golangci-lint revive checks (naming, exported docs, etc.).

quote: misspell is left out on purpose: comments here are bilingual, and it reports Portuguese words such as "algoritmos" or "processos" as misspelled English.
statement: In Go files under the root config, the misspell linter is deliberately not enabled.

quote: enable: - misspell; settings: misspell: ignore-rules: [problemas, candidatas, componentes, algoritmos]
statement: In several Go mini-project modules (lru-bloom-trie, rate-limiter, graph-algorithms, nand-alu-cpu, deadlock-mini-shell, ...), misspell is enabled with ignore-rules listing Portuguese/Spanish comment words.

quote: No abstractions for single-use code.
statement: In all code, abstractions must not be introduced for single-use code.

quote: Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
statement: In changed code, imports, variables and functions made unused by the change must be removed.

quote: No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
statement: In all code, there must be no interface with a single implementation, no factory for a single product, and no config for a value that never changes.

quote: Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path
statement: In all code, deliberate simplifications with a known ceiling must be marked with a `ponytail: <ceiling>, <upgrade path>` comment.

quote: Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind
statement: Non-trivial logic (branches, loops, parsers, money/security paths) must have at least one runnable check (an assert-based self-check or a small test).

quote: **Separate data fetching from presentation:**
statement: In React UIs, data fetching should live in container components/hooks separate from presentational components.

quote: **Avoid prop drilling deeper than 3 levels.**
statement: In React UIs, props should not be drilled through more than 3 component levels; use context or restructure.

quote: Don't skip heading levels. Don't use heading styles for non-heading content.
statement: In UI markup, heading levels must not be skipped and heading elements must not be used for non-heading content.

quote: Use semantic color tokens: `text-primary`, `bg-surface`, `border-default` — not raw hex values
statement: In UI styling, colours must use semantic tokens rather than raw hex values.

quote:
// Every interactive element must be keyboard accessible ...
Click me
// ✗ Not focusable
statement: In UI markup, interactive elements must be keyboard accessible: use <button> rather than a <div onClick> without role and tabIndex.

quote: **Don't mix patterns.** If some endpoints throw, others return null, and others return `{ error }` — the consumer can't predict behavior.
statement: In APIs, error reporting must follow one consistent pattern (not a mix of throwing, returning null and returning { error }).

quote: **Derive the key from the intent, not the attempt.** The key must be stable across retries of one intent and different across distinct intents
statement: In idempotent operations, the idempotency key must be derived from the intent (client-supplied or immutable id), not crypto.randomUUID() or Date.now() per attempt.

quote: // ✓ let the unique constraint pick the winner
statement: In idempotency handling, the key must be claimed atomically via a unique constraint rather than a read-then-write check (TOCTOU).

quote: **Guard the payload.** Same key with a different body is a client bug, and must fail loudly rather than serving the first response to a second request
statement: In idempotency handling, a reused key with a different payload must be rejected with an error.

quote: ### Use Discriminated Unions for Variants
statement: In TypeScript, variant types should be modelled as discriminated unions with a type tag.

quote: ### Use Branded Types for IDs
statement: In TypeScript, entity IDs should use branded types (string & { readonly __brand: ... }).

quote: Every endpoint has typed input and output schemas
statement: In API code, every endpoint must have typed input and output schemas.

quote: List endpoints support pagination
statement: In API code, list endpoints must support pagination.

quote: Parameterize every query. Never build SQL, NoSQL, or shell commands from input strings.
statement: In all code, database queries and shell commands must be parameterized and never built by concatenating input strings.
scope: all source files with DB or shell access

quote: Hash passwords with bcrypt (≥12 rounds), scrypt, or argon2. The session secret comes from the environment, never from code.
statement: In auth code, passwords must be hashed with bcrypt (>=12 rounds), scrypt or argon2, and session secrets must come from the environment, not source code.

quote: Session cookies are `httpOnly`, `secure`, and `sameSite: 'lax'` or `'strict'` ... with a bounded `maxAge`.
statement: In session code, session cookies must be set with httpOnly, secure, sameSite 'lax' or 'strict', and a bounded maxAge.

quote: **Never log sensitive data** (passwords, tokens, full credit card numbers)
statement: In all code, log statements must not include passwords, tokens or full card numbers.

quote: **Never use `eval()` or `innerHTML`** with user-provided data
statement: In all code, eval() and innerHTML must not be used with user-provided data.

quote: **Never store sessions in client-accessible storage** (localStorage for auth tokens)
statement: In client code, auth/session tokens must not be stored in localStorage or other client-accessible storage.

quote: **Never expose stack traces** or internal error details to users
statement: In HTTP handlers, error responses must not expose stack traces or internal error details.

quote: Check **authorization** on every request, not just authentication: the authenticated user must own, or be permitted on, the specific resource (A01, IDOR).
statement: In protected handlers, every request must check authorization on the specific resource, not only authentication.

quote: Security headers on every response (helmet or the framework equivalent); CSP starts from `default-src 'self'` and is tightened, not loosened.
statement: In HTTP servers, every response must carry security headers, with a CSP starting from default-src 'self'.

quote: CORS restricted to an explicit origin list from configuration. Never `*` with credentials.
statement: In HTTP servers, CORS must use an explicit origin list from configuration and never '*' together with credentials.

quote: Strip sensitive fields (`passwordHash`, reset tokens) before any response. Error bodies are generic; internals go to server logs only.
statement: In HTTP handlers, sensitive fields such as passwordHash and reset tokens must be stripped from responses, and error bodies must be generic.

quote: Server-side URL fetches validated against an allowlist (no SSRF)
statement: In server code, fetches of user-supplied URLs must be validated against an allowlist.

quote: | Nested ternaries | Requires mental stack to parse | Replace with if/else chains, switch, or lookup objects |
statement: In all code, nested ternary expressions should be replaced with if/else, switch or lookup objects.

quote: | Boolean parameter flags | `doThing(true, false, true)` | Replace with options objects or separate functions |
statement: In all code, functions should not take positional boolean flag parameters; use an options object or separate functions.

quote: | Abbreviated names | `usr`, `cfg`, `btn`, `evt` | Use full words unless the abbreviation is universal (`id`, `url`, `api`) |
statement: In all code, identifiers should use full words rather than abbreviations like usr, cfg, btn, evt (except universal ones such as id, url, api).

quote: | Redundant type assertions | Casting to a type that's already inferred | Remove the assertion |
statement: In TypeScript code, redundant type assertions to an already-inferred type should be removed.

quote: Labels must come from small, fixed sets (route template, status class, provider name). Never use user IDs, raw URLs, error messages, or other unbounded values as labels
statement: In metrics code, metric labels must come from small fixed sets and must not use user IDs, raw URLs, error messages or other unbounded values.

quote: All log output is structured (JSON), with stable event names and a correlation ID on every line
statement: In service code, logs must be structured JSON with stable event names and a correlation ID, not ad-hoc console.log output.

quote: Latency is a histogram; p95/p99 are queryable
statement: In metrics code, latency must be recorded as a histogram.

quote: ### Prefer Real Implementations Over Mocks
statement: In tests, real implementations should be preferred over fakes, stubs and mocks; mock only at slow or non-deterministic boundaries.

quote: Test names describe the behavior being verified
statement: In tests, test names must describe the behavior being verified.

quote: No N+1 patterns
statement: In data-access code, queries must not follow N+1 patterns (one query per item in a loop).

quote: Every input that changes the response belongs in the key (tenant, locale, permissions, feature flags) ... Never cache what must be fresh (balances, permissions, inventory at checkout).
statement: In caching code, cache keys must include every input that changes the response, and values that must be fresh (balances, permissions, checkout inventory) must not be cached.
